recognition.identity: UCI Online Shoppers Purchasing Intention Dataset (UCI ID 468), identified from the supplied metadata.
recognition.basis: Dataset recognition comes from the bundle; no independent retrieval or analysis was performed.

candidate.title: Does product-duration share add information beyond browsing volume?
candidate.question: Among sessions with positive total recorded duration, does ProductRelated_Duration divided by the sum of the three supplied duration fields improve held-out prediction of Revenue beyond page counts, total recorded duration, and supplied context? What is the model-based probability contrast between the training-fold 25th and 75th percentiles of this share at median ProductRelated count?

core.object: Session-level share of recorded duration attributed to product-related pages.
core.relation_or_action: Compare identical held-out splits for logistic models with and without product-duration share and its interaction with ProductRelated count; exclude PageValues.
core.contrast: Baseline versus augmented model; separately report the augmented model's predicted probability contrast across training-fold share quartiles.
core.prediction: The augmented model will modestly improve held-out log loss and show a positive modeled contrast.
core.independent_unit: Session, as described in the supplied dataset metadata.

candidate.failure_condition: No reproducible paired log-loss improvement, or the modeled contrast is uncertain across both directions.
assumptions: The three duration fields can be summed for this descriptive share.
The share measures recorded duration composition, not attention or a causal lever.
Session-level splitting is appropriate for this within-dataset feasibility analysis but does not establish future deployment performance.
candidate.required_new_data: Event-level timestamps and a defined prediction time to assess feature availability before purchase; external sessions for deployment validation.
candidate.domain_value: Tests whether analytics distinguish duration composition from browsing volume without implying that changing browsing behavior would change purchases.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Conditions product-duration share on page counts and total duration, then reports a supported model-based contrast rather than a single feature association.

final.what_changed: Clarified the share denominator, specified that zero-total-duration sessions must be counted and reported separately, and narrowed interpretation to recorded-duration composition. The requested computation returned a clarification because external I/O/dynamic execution was prohibited, so no metrics or prevalence estimates were produced. The search returned general purchase-prediction work, not a direct test of this conditional allocation contrast.
final.what_is_known: The bundle supplies 12,330 sessions and documents the duration fields and Revenue. It does not provide results for the proposed comparison. Compute request compute_0 did not execute. Search result search_1 was limited Crossref metadata; it does not establish whether close prior work exists.
final.new_hypothesis: None supported by returned evidence. The original positive-association and predictive-improvement forecast remains an untested proposal.
final.next_falsifiable_test: Execute the prespecified paired repeated stratified cross-validation comparison; report zero-total-duration count, paired held-out log-loss differences, and uncertainty and support for the share-quartile probability contrast. Separately obtain event timing or external data before making claims about decision-time availability or deployment.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The returned 2026 paper concerns conversion-prediction and decision-support performance on this dataset. Its abstract does not report the conditional product-duration-share contrast proposed here. The dataset's 2019 introduction paper is also identified in the supplied metadata as prediction-focused. These records do not establish novelty or exclude closer work.
final.novelty_status: Unverified; the limited search found no direct overlap in the returned abstracts, which is not evidence of a literature gap.
